clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute transverse myelitis (ATM) in the context of recent COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man presented 18 days after confirmed COVID-19 infection (positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR) with progressive bilateral lower limb weakness, urinary retention, constipation, and a sensory level at T10 (umbilicus) with upper motor neuron signs. MRI spine on admission demonstrated longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) with T2 hyperintensity from T7-T10 without enhancement or mass. CSF analysis revealed elevated protein (0.79 g/L) with normal glucose and negative bacterial cultures. SARS-CoV-2 PCR was negative in CSF. Serum testing excluded neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (negative AQP4-IgG, MOG-IgG) and other demyelinating conditions. Infectious workup was negative for EBV, CMV, HIV, hepatitis B/C, and mycoplasma. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g/day for 3 days. By day 10, repeat MRI showed almost complete resolution of spinal cord signal changes, and by day 11 the patient achieved full motor recovery, resolution of paresthesias, successful catheter removal, and discharge home.
